observations: Loop 3 used only deterministic fake platform, fake ticket-recognition, and protected scheduling fixtures.
No real Chengfeng host, account, credential, browser profile, request, production image, or platform write was used.
No legacy project, database, browser profile, launcher, runtime, port, or running legacy process was attached to, executed, reused, stopped, or changed.
The browser validation used an isolated temporary data root and the loopback target http://127.0.0.1:8877.
Every request observed during browser validation used 127.0.0.1; console errors and warnings were both zero.
No Windows DNS, proxy, VPN, routing, hosts file, or global browser setting was changed.
No real PaddleOCR, CPU OCR, GPU OCR, CUDA runtime, OCR model, or production document was loaded.
Protected Loop 3 exercises require an explicit enable-test-fixtures startup gate and an explicit data root.
Every protected exercise is classified as test_fixture and keeps business_outcome null.
The shared evidence identity includes both the image SHA-256 and pipeline fingerprint.
The existing OCR boundary test continued to verify that platform expected weights are not supplied to the recognition adapter.
A technical fake OCR failure remains a system failure and is not converted into a finance-review item.
The local API contains no settlement confirmation, payment, receipt cancellation, automatic ticket swap, or other Chengfeng write endpoint.
